newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker after Greenspan.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply down on Wednesday as U.S. interest rates soared in the wake of what traders said was hawkish testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan.
"The peso came under pressure when soaring U.S. interest rates prompted local dealers to cover short dollar positions and some foreigners to bale out of Mexico," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 3.9 and 3.7 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8010/7.8040 and 7.7970/7.8000 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.2 centavos weaker at 7.7730/7.7760 per dollar.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds climbed to 6.80 percent from 6.65 percent on Tuesday.

Traders put the sharp increase in U.S. long bond yields down to Senate testimony by Alan Greenspan in which he suggested the Federal Reserve may need to raise U.S. rates in order to contain inflationary pressures.
"We expect this to be absorbed by the market over the next few days," another trader said.
Dealers said the peso had also been hit by month-end corporate demand for dollars and the tenth consecutive fall in primary rates at Tuesday night's weekly auction.
"The sharp fall in interest rates came as quite a surprise after the central bank drained so much liquidity from the secondary market yesterday," a dealer said.
"Furthermore, we had the usual month-end demand for dollars," he added.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 27-day Cetes rates at 18.59 percent at its primary auction, a fall of 87 basis points. Money market traders previously surveyed by Reuters had forecast an average fall of just 60 basis points.
Dealers said they expected the peso to weaken further against the dollar on Thursday. ((--Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
